ozet: The Prophet's years in trade, the journey to Syria with Khadija's caravan, his marriage to Khadija and their children; Zayd ibn Haritha and 'Ali join the household.

b08-s01: In his youth the Prophet worked in trade. He went to the fair of Hubasha in Yemen and to the fairs of Suhar and Daba.
Everyone who knew him knew him to be truthful and trustworthy. Even before he became a prophet, Quraysh called him 'al-Amin', that is, 'the trustworthy one'.
b08-s02: In Mecca there was a noble and wealthy lady named Khadija, the daughter of Khuwaylid.
Khadija sent men to trade with her goods and shared the profit with them. She had been married twice before and had lost both husbands.
b08-s03: Khadija heard how truthful and trustworthy the Prophet was. She offered him to take her goods to Syria and trade with them.
She would give him more than she gave other merchants. Her servant Maysara would go with him.
b08-s04: The Prophet accepted the offer. Together with Maysara he joined the caravan and set out for Syria.
b08-s05: According to the reports, when they reached the land of Syria, they stopped in the shade of a tree near a monk's monastery.
The monk asked Maysara who the man resting under the tree was, and said: 'No one but a prophet has ever stopped beneath this tree.'
b08-s06: In Syria the Prophet sold the goods he had brought, bought what he wished to buy, and returned to Mecca.
Khadija sold the goods that were brought back; the profit was double, or close to it.
b08-s07: Some time later Khadija sent word to the Prophet.
She told him that she wished to marry him because of their kinship, his honoured place among his people, his trustworthiness, his fine character and his truthfulness.
b08-s08: The Prophet told his uncles of this offer. His uncles went and asked her family for Khadija's hand.
b08-s09: And so they were married. As the bridal gift the Prophet gave twenty young she-camels.
The Prophet was twenty-five years old at the time. Khadija is reported to have been about forty.
b08-s10: Khadija was the Prophet's first wife. As long as she lived, he married no one else.

All his children except Ibrahim were from Khadija. His daughters were Zaynab, Ruqayya, Umm Kulthum and Fatima. The names of his sons appear in the reports as al-Qasim, 'Abdullah, al-Tayyib and al-Tahir.
Their first child was al-Qasim. The Prophet came to be called 'Abu al-Qasim', meaning 'the father of al-Qasim'. Al-Qasim died young.
All his sons died before the Prophet became a prophet. His daughters, however, lived to see Islam, became Muslims and emigrated with him.
b08-s11: After the marriage a young man named Zayd ibn Haritha joined the household.
Zayd was of the Kalb tribe. As a child, while travelling with his mother to visit relatives, he had been kidnapped and sold as a slave.
Khadija's nephew Hakim ibn Hizam had brought some slaves. Khadija chose Zayd from among them. The Prophet asked Khadija for Zayd, and she gave him to him.
b08-s12: Zayd's father Haritha had grieved deeply over the loss of his son. At last he learned where he was and came to Mecca.
The Prophet left the choice to Zayd: if he wished, he could go with his father. But Zayd chose to stay with the Prophet.
b08-s13: The Prophet freed Zayd and adopted him.
From then on Zayd was known as 'Zayd ibn Muhammad', until the verse came down commanding that adopted children be called by the names of their own fathers.
b08-s14: One year a severe famine struck Quraysh. Abu Talib's family was large, and making a living had become hard for him.
The Prophet spoke with his uncle al-'Abbas, the wealthiest of the sons of Hashim. To lighten Abu Talib's burden, each of them would take one of his children.
The Prophet took 'Ali, and al-'Abbas took Ja'far. 'Ali stayed with the Prophet all the way until he became a prophet.
b08-s15: Even after Khadija's death, the Messenger of Allah always remembered her. He would say that she believed when no one else believed, that she affirmed him when people called him a liar, that she supported him with her wealth when no one else gave anything, and that Allah gave him children through her.
